name: data/audit-log
summary: Record security-relevant actions in an append-oriented audit trail without leaking secrets.
intent: Sensitive administrative or account-changing actions produce durable audit events with enough actor, action, target, time, and request context to investigate what happened while secrets and private payloads remain excluded.

rules.text: Each opted-in security-relevant action emits one structured audit event after its outcome is known.
Audit events capture the authenticated actor when available, action type, target identity, timestamp, outcome, and a request or trace correlation identifier.
Normal application code appends audit events rather than editing historical events in place.
The application has an explicit policy for audit-write failure so a lost event is not silently mistaken for successful auditing.

invariants.text: The audit trail records domain/security events without replacing operational logs, metrics, or the authoritative domain data.
Audit instrumentation does not change the domain result except where the host explicitly chooses fail-closed behavior for mandatory auditing.
Existing application logging remains usable and is not duplicated wholesale into the audit store.

security.text: Passwords, session secrets, tokens, private keys, raw authentication assertions, and similarly sensitive payloads are never stored in audit event fields.
Reading or exporting audit events is restricted to explicitly authorized server-side roles or processes.
Actor identity and privileged context are derived from trusted server-side authentication state rather than user-supplied audit fields.
Storage and retention choices make unauthorized deletion or modification materially harder than changing ordinary application output.

acceptance.text: A successful opted-in sensitive action produces one audit event with actor, action, target, outcome, time, and correlation context.
A failed opted-in action records the intended failure outcome without falsely recording a successful change.
Representative secret or credential values used by the action do not appear in the stored audit event.
An unauthorized application user cannot read or export the audit trail through the introduced interface.
